title: SERIALIZABLE and retries
objective: Specify a retry classifier that re-runs a whole command after a serialization failure or a deadlock, never after an out-of-range value or a typed refusal, bounds the attempts and logs each one by its error code, and stamp the claim that retries terminate as assumed, with its reason.

segments.title: Retry the decision, not the statement

blocks.md: SERIALIZABLE makes concurrent transactions behave as if they ran one at a time (§13.2.3, read 2026-10-23). It does that by aborting a transaction that would break the illusion, and your application sees an error. Retrying is a design decision: which errors, how often, and what you tell the caller when you stop.

choice.prompt: Txn B's hold insert failed at COMMIT with a serialization failure. What should the runtime retry?

options.text: The COMMIT, where the failure was raised.
options.why: The transaction ended when the commit failed, and its decision rests on stale reads.

options.text: The whole command from BEGIN, deciding again.
options.why: The manual says "It is important to retry the complete transaction, including all logic that decides which SQL to issue and/or which values to use" (§13.5, read 2026-10-23).

options.text: The INSERT alone, keeping the earlier reads.
options.why: The earlier reads are what went stale.

options.text: Nothing: the failure means the command is wrong.
options.why: A serialization failure reports a conflict with another transaction, not a bug in the command.

blocks.md: Replay S6.L6's holds history at SERIALIZABLE, with txn B retrying after its failure. Make your call first.
The holds history at SERIALIZABLE, with txn B retried from BEGIN (catalog row H23).
blocks.direction: Replay shows: txn A commits, txn B's first attempt fails at COMMIT, and its retry begins a new transaction.

call.prompt: Txn B retries the whole command from BEGIN. The retry now returns:

options.text: Committed: a second hold of 80 is placed.
options.why: The retry reads again and now sees 20 available, not 100.

options.text: A serialization failure again, as before.
options.why: Txn A has committed, so the retry does not overlap it.

options.text: A deadlock with the committed txn A.
options.why: Nothing waits on a lock, so there is no cycle.

options.text: Refused by its own guard, and nothing is written.
options.why: Only 20 is available, so the guard refuses. The retry gives the serial answer, the one txn B would have got after txn A.

blocks.after: The retry decided again from what is true now {{run:RUN-pg-catalog}} (row H23). The answer changed from "insert a hold" to "refuse", and only a retry that re-reads can notice.

blocks.md:
Decide by error code, and write the decision down as data. The codes are PostgreSQL's SQLSTATEs (https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/errcodes-appendix.html).

| Error | What it means | What the runtime does |
|---|---|---|
| 40001 | serialization failure | Retry the whole command from BEGIN. |
| 40P01 | deadlock detected | Retry the whole command from BEGIN. |
| 23505, 23P01 | unique or exclusion violation | Retry only inside a command that re-reads the key before it writes, a bounded number of times. Never re-send the same blind insert. |
| 22003 | value out of range | Never retry: the same input fails again. |
| `Insufficient`, `NoSuchAccount` | typed refusals | Never retry: they are outcomes. |

The rule for unique and exclusion violations is this course's choice, because the code alone does not say whether the condition persists. The manual warns they "might represent persistent error conditions rather than transient failures" (§13.5).

Under SERIALIZABLE a retry that re-checked the key ended without an error, and a blind retry failed with the same code again (rows H12a and H12b {{run:RUN-pg-catalog}}).

Bound the attempts by k, with a jittered pause. When k is spent, return `GaveUp`, an outcome your reference semantics lacks, which S6.L8's relation has to place. Let nothing leave your system before COMMIT: data read is not valid "until the transaction which read it has successfully committed" (§13.2.3).

Does a retry loop end? The manual does not promise it: "Transaction retry does not guarantee that the retried transaction will complete; multiple retries may be needed" (§13.5). So "retries terminate" is a claim you can state and cannot establish. Stamp it ASSUMED [A], with its reason: contention is assumed finite and below the budget. Attempt logs support it on the runs they cover.

choice.prompt: A command's attempt log: attempt 1 ended in a deadlock error, attempt 2 in an out-of-range error. What does the policy do next?

options.text: Retry: both errors might clear on a new attempt.
options.why: A deadlock might. An out-of-range error will not: the same input fails the same way.

options.text: Stop: the out-of-range error is final and is returned.
options.why: The policy retries a deadlock and never an out-of-range error.
`GaveUp` means the budget ran out on errors that might clear. This error is final at once.

options.text: Retry only the failed statement, not the command.
options.why: The whole command is retried, never one statement, and here nothing is retried.

choice.prompt: An attempt log over n commands shows at most m attempts per command, always below the budget, and no `GaveUp`. The claim: retries terminate. Which stamp fits?

options.why: A log records runs. No number of runs establishes the next one.
That fits "these n commands terminated", a different proposition.
Nothing explored the loop exhaustively. The log recorded runs.
The claim rests on contention staying finite and below the budget, which no log establishes.

blocks.title: Reading
blocks.md: Your roadmap's Stage 6 reading is PostgreSQL's chapter on transaction isolation. Here, read §13.5, "Serialization Failure Handling" (https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/mvcc-serialization-failure-handling.html, read 2026-10-23), and §13.2.3 (https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/transaction-iso.html, read 2026-10-23). Optional: Ports and Grittner, "Serializable Snapshot Isolation in PostgreSQL", PVLDB 5(12), 2012, §5.4.

blocks.title: Build this
blocks.md: Next, write the retry classifier from the table and run it on the attempt logs. It must log each attempt by error code, never retry out-of-range errors, and stop at your k with `GaveUp`.

RUN-pg-catalog.title: PostgreSQL 18.6 isolation catalog: rows H01-H24 in isolationtester format, the upstream baseline, the SERIALIZABLE behavior of 40001, 40P01, 23505 and 23P01, and the seeded GEN-anomaly-id grid

budget.data_directory: tmpfs, 2g (a speed choice; visibility rules do not depend on it)
budget.network: default bridge, unused during the runs
budget.step_timeout: PG_TEST_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT=10 (the tester cancels a step after 20 s and exits after 40 s); 2 for the one-permutation fallback
budget.cpu: no cap; other tasks used the host at the same time, so durations are noisy

ROW H01 [agrees]: READ COMMITTED: both commit, final 20, the second debit's write returns 20 -> 20. SERIALIZABLE, only expected before, is recorded: 40001.
ROW H02 [agrees]: READ COMMITTED: the waiting statement updates 0 rows. REPEATABLE READ and SERIALIZABLE, only expected before, are recorded: 40001.
ROW H03 [agrees]: READ COMMITTED: the DELETE removes 0 rows and a hits = 10 row exists before and after. REPEATABLE READ and SERIALIZABLE: 40001.
ROW H04 [agrees]: The reader's two reads total 250 at READ COMMITTED and 200 at REPEATABLE READ and SERIALIZABLE.
ROW H05 [agrees]: Both commit at READ COMMITTED and REPEATABLE READ with a team total of -100; at SERIALIZABLE the second committer fails with 40001 and the total is 50.
ROW H06 [agrees]: Both commit at READ COMMITTED and REPEATABLE READ (160 held against 100); at SERIALIZABLE one fails with 40001 and 80 stays held.
ROW H07 [agrees]: Run from the upstream specs: REPEATABLE READ gives s3 a state no serial order shows; SERIALIZABLE aborts s2 with 40001 (-2); DEFERRABLE makes s3 wait (-3).
ROW H08 [agrees]: 6 of 210 permutations fail with s3 READ ONLY; the READ WRITE variant is measured here, not read from the spec comment.
ROW H09 [agrees]: The second count is 3 at READ COMMITTED, 2 at REPEATABLE READ and SERIALIZABLE.
ROW H10 [agrees]: With one session SERIALIZABLE and the other READ COMMITTED both commit, in both assignments and both commit orders; with both SERIALIZABLE one fails with 40001.
ROW H11 [agrees]: A sequential scan aborts a SERIALIZABLE transaction that shares no row with the other; the same transactions on an index scan over distant keys both commit.

ROW H12 [agrees, with additions]: 23505 and 23P01 appear under SERIALIZABLE; which of 40001 and 23505 appears depends on whether the failing session checked first and on the order, and a whole-command retry with a re-check ends without error where a blind retry fails again.
ROW H13 [agrees]: READ COMMITTED: the statement waits, then updates the row it could not see. REPEATABLE READ and SERIALIZABLE: 40001.
ROW H14 [agrees]: READ COMMITTED: 23505, no restart. REPEATABLE READ: 23505. SERIALIZABLE: 40001.
ROW H15 [agrees]: Disjoint claims at all three levels; the count through SKIP LOCKED is 0 while 4 jobs are pending.
ROW H16 [agrees]: READ COMMITTED returns the rows out of order; REPEATABLE READ and SERIALIZABLE raise 40001; FOR UPDATE in a subquery returns them in order.
ROW H17 [agrees]: READ COMMITTED: mallory sees 'secret from mallory'. REPEATABLE READ and SERIALIZABLE: her locking read fails with 40001, so it is prevented by failure.
ROW H18 [agrees]: CHECK accepts NULL, the guarded UPDATE skips the NULL row, USING hides it, WITH CHECK raises 42501; the same at all three levels.
ROW H19 [agrees]: 22003 'bigint out of range' at all three levels; the balance is unchanged; sum(bigint) is numeric.
ROW H20 [agrees]: Row 1 is never delivered: the mark is 2, both ids exist, the next poll returns nothing; the same at all three levels.
ROW H21 [agrees]: Both permutations of the regression test end with bar's 40001, the output the upstream file expects.

ROW H22 [differs]: Ascending order removes the deadlock and both commit at READ COMMITTED. At REPEATABLE READ and SERIALIZABLE, 4 of the 6 ascending-order permutations still fail with 40001 (first updater wins), so ordering is no substitute for the retry.
ROW H23 [agrees]: B's COMMIT fails with 40001; its retry reads 20 available, the guard refuses (0 rows) and nothing is written.
ROW H24 [agrees]: REPEATABLE READ and SERIALIZABLE: B fails with 40001 and its retry updates 0 rows. READ COMMITTED: no error, 0 rows.
notes: The tester is PostgreSQL's own isolationtester, built from the 18.6 source tarball and run against the Debian-packaged 18.6 server of the postgres:18 image; it is not statespace isorun (W4-T16).

isolationtester prints errors as 'ERROR:  <message>' without a SQLSTATE. SQLSTATEs come from the server's csv log: each session's application_name is '<tag>/<session>', and for every session the messages the tester printed must equal the messages the server logged, in order; a mismatch stops the run.
NULL prints as an empty cell in isolationtester output; an empty string prints the same way.

A session that continues after an error meets 'current transaction is aborted' (25P02) at its next write. Those follow-on errors stay in the row outputs, as after_abort in the index, and keep a history out of the GEN-anomaly-id pool.
The lock model that decides which interleavings cannot hang the tester is sound and incomplete; every lock wait the tester reported was one the model predicted.
The grid's 'half' split, the target counts and the retry patterns are design defaults [D], not measurements.
Nothing was emulated: no browser, phone, hosted service or other PostgreSQL version was involved. PGlite is a different instrument (W0-S08).
